description: Single source of truth for AutoFlow's per-phase spawn policy (model + effort). Read it with scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh; never restate its values in prose (CLAUDE.md > Spawn Model — Phase-by-Phase).
sample_contract: This file is a SAMPLE carrying the values currently applied, not a universal vocabulary the framework enforces. It ships as a `scaffold` artifact: a stamp/install creates it only when absent and never overwrites it (not even under --force), so the values here are the target's to configure at stamp time and afterwards. On a version bump, run `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` and add any newly required row — an outdated scaffold is a diagnosable state, since both deliberation workflows fail closed on a missing required workflow_sites row, and the architect deliberation additionally fails closed on a missing deliberation_caps row (its turn ceilings live here too, not as code literals).

effort_contract.is_the_vocabulary_check_applies: `scripts/spawn-policy/spawn-policy.sh check` reads its admitted effort vocabulary and its inherit sentinel from THIS object, so `check` is a self-consistency check over one source. A runtime with a different effort vocabulary is accommodated by editing this contract, never by patching the checker; model values are deliberately unvalidated beyond presence and shape
effort_contract.admitted_one_spelling_per_level: both harness channels run the same coercion, which also accepts the alias "med" for "medium"; this policy admits one spelling per level, so "med" is deliberately not admitted here
effort_contract.sentinel_is_config_only: "inherit" is this file's own vocabulary and is never written to either harness channel: a Workflow agent() opts object omits the effort key, and an agent-definition frontmatter omits the effort line
effort_contract.absent_means: identical to "inherit" — the row declares no override and the spawn inherits the session effort. A row carrying no effort key at all is a validation error, not an inherit: `spawn-policy.sh check` rejects it, so a misspelled key surfaces in the tree rather than reading as policy

policy_unmapped_agent_types.autoflow-planner: no phase in the policy spawns this type — ARCHITECT is Workflow facilitation, so its design work has no direct-spawn row; the definition ships for ad-hoc planning spawns outside the phase policy

diagnose-intake-triage.work_type: new-issue readiness pre-filter (planning/design/ADR prerequisite), no code tools

diagnose-loopcheck.work_type: review-response loop check — prior-cycle complaint-class comparison

diagnose-phase-3.work_type: necessity scoring (Behavior gap + Code-change lever; reuse-neutral)

red.work_type: acceptance criteria → test code (complex tests fall back to the higher tier, with rationale in the Test AI report)

green.work_type: minimum implementation that passes the tests

handoff-review-triage.work_type: reviewer-comment ingestion (severity classification) + Low-finding impact judgment

deliberation_caps.semantics: Turn ceilings for the turn-based deliberation loop (issue #152): a turn is ONE participant's review (Test AI and Developer AI alternate), so one exchange = two turns. max_turns bounds a cold run; bounded_max_turns bounds a scope-bounded review-response run; a resume admits exactly one further exchange (two turns) past the persisted turn count, in code, and reads neither value. Both values are integers >= 2 — the termination condition pairs a turn with its predecessor, so a ceiling below one full exchange could never converge. The workflow fails closed (verdict ESCALATE, sentinel 'spawn policy deliberation caps incomplete') when its row here is missing or malformed.
